first.rationale: Onboarding completion and activation are both declining, and prior evidence indicates shortened, simplified self-serve onboarding improves completion, time-to-value, and early activation—leading indicators of sustainable qualified revenue. Verify memory_86 because it directly supports the chosen intervention; verify memory_73 because competitor pricing makes promotional pricing the most consequential alternative, but its long-term revenue quality and discount durability need scrutiny before displacing an activation-focused experiment.

mid.rationale: Run a standard experiment simplifying and shortening self-serve onboarding. The verified prior experiment improved completion by 13%, reduced time-to-value by 2.1 days, and increased 30-day retention by 3%, directly addressing both current completion and activation declines while supporting durable qualified revenue. Do not use broad discounting: its verified acquisition lift was paired with a 12% retention decline and failure to survive the first renewal cycle.

final2.rationale: Keep the onboarding-simplification experiment. It directly addresses the concurrent declines in completion and activation and has verified durable signals: +13% completion, 2.1 fewer days to value, and +3% 30-day retention. The deeper competitor cut increases urgency but does not make broad promotional pricing sustainable: the verified targeted-discount cohort had -12% 30-day retention and did not survive first renewal. Monitor price-sensitive SMB churn separately, but do not replace a retention-supporting experiment with a discount-led response that is known to degrade downstream value.
